items.lesson_concept: The right to privacy is anchored in Article III, Section 3 of the 1987 Constitution, establishing the inviolability of privacy of communication and correspondence.
items.question_text: Which constitutional provision protects the privacy of communication and correspondence in the Philippines?
items.correct_answer: Article III, Section 3
items.explanation: Article III, Section 3 guarantees that privacy of communication and correspondence shall be inviolable except upon lawful order of the court or public safety.

items.lesson_concept: Republic Act No. 10173 is formally known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012, enacted to protect individual personal information while fostering information flows.
items.question_text: What is the official short title of Republic Act No. 10173?
items.correct_answer: Data Privacy Act of 2012
items.explanation: Republic Act No. 10173 is entitled the Data Privacy Act of 2012 (DPA).

items.lesson_concept: The National Privacy Commission (NPC) is an independent body attached to the DICT for policy coordination, tasked with monitoring and enforcing compliance with RA 10173.
items.question_text: To which government department is the National Privacy Commission attached for policy coordination?
options: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG)
items.correct_answer: Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)
items.explanation: Under RA 10173 Section 7, the NPC is attached to the DICT strictly for policy and program coordination.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA applies extraterritorially to processing outside the country if it relates to Philippine citizens/residents, uses equipment located in the country, or has an office/branch locally.
items.question_text: A foreign enterprise with zero physical presence in the Philippines processes data of Filipino citizens residing in Cebu. Does the DPA apply?
options: No, the DPA is strictly territorial.
Yes, the DPA applies extraterritorially to processing involving Philippine citizens or residents.
No, unless authorized by an international treaty.
Yes, but only if the enterprise operates a local branch.
items.correct_answer: Yes, the DPA applies extraterritorially to processing involving Philippine citizens or residents.
items.explanation: Section 6 of the DPA establishes extraterritorial application when processing relates to Philippine citizens or residents.

items.lesson_concept: Section 4 of RA 10173 excludes information about officers/employees of government institutions relating to their position or official functions.
items.question_text: A citizen requests the official salary grade and job description of an Undersecretary under Freedom of Information. Can the agency withhold it citing the DPA?
options: Yes, employee financial data is always confidential.
No, information relating to the position or official functions of government officers is excluded from the DPA.
Yes, unless approved by the NPC.
No, but only if the Undersecretary gives written consent.
items.correct_answer: No, information relating to the position or official functions of government officers is excluded from the DPA.
items.explanation: Section 4(a) excludes information about any individual who is or was an officer or employee of a government institution relating to their official functions.

items.lesson_concept: Personal information processed for journalistic, artistic, literary, or research purposes is exempt from the DPA, provided published work adheres to ethical guidelines.
items.question_text: An investigative journalist writes an article exposing public corruption using legitimately gathered source materials. The official claims a DPA violation. How does the law apply?
options: The journalist is liable for unauthorized processing.
The processing is excluded under Section 4 for journalistic purposes.
The journalist must obtain NPC pre-clearance.
The DPA completely overrides journalistic freedom.
items.correct_answer: The processing is excluded under Section 4 for journalistic purposes.
items.explanation: Section 4(d) of the DPA excludes personal information processed for journalistic, artistic, literary, or research purposes.

items.lesson_concept: Personal information originally collected from foreign residents in accordance with their local laws and processed in the Philippines is excluded from the DPA under Section 4(g).
items.question_text: A Philippine BPO processes health insurance records of German citizens for a client in Berlin under the GDPR. Under Section 4(g) of the DPA, what is the status of this data?
options: Fully subject to DPA instead of GDPR.
Excluded from the scope of the DPA as foreign resident data processed under foreign law.
Subject to automatic NPC breach reporting.
items.correct_answer: Excluded from the scope of the DPA as foreign resident data processed under foreign law.
items.explanation: Section 4(g) excludes personal information originally collected from residents of foreign jurisdictions in accordance with foreign laws processed locally.

items.lesson_concept: Personal Information (PI) is any data from which the identity of an individual is apparent or can be reasonably and directly ascertained.
items.question_text: Which of the following constitutes standard Personal Information (PI) under the DPA?
items.correct_answer: Full name and residential address
items.explanation: Full name and residential address identify an individual directly without falling into special sensitive categories.

items.lesson_concept: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) includes race, marital status, age, religious/political affiliations, health, education, genetic data, sexual life, and government IDs.
items.question_text: Which of the following is explicitly classified as Sensitive Personal Information?
items.correct_answer: Social Security System (SSS) number
items.explanation: Government-issued identification numbers unique to an individual (such as SSS, TIN, and passport numbers) are SPI under Section 3(l).

items.lesson_concept: Privileged Information refers to any and all forms of data which under the Rules of Court and other pertinent laws constitute privileged communication (e.g., attorney-client, doctor-patient).
items.question_text: What is the legal classification of confidential communications exchanged between an attorney and their client under the DPA?
items.correct_answer: Privileged Information
items.explanation: Privileged information refers to data protected under the Rules of Court regarding privileged communication.

items.lesson_concept: A Personal Information Controller (PIC) controls the processing and instructs others, while a Personal Information Processor (PIP) merely processes data on behalf of a PIC.
items.question_text: An enterprise outsources its payroll computations to an independent accounting firm under explicit contractual parameters. What role does the accounting firm assume?
items.correct_answer: Personal Information Processor (PIP)
items.explanation: The accounting firm acts as a PIP because it processes data strictly on the instructions and behalf of the client enterprise (the PIC).

items.lesson_concept: An entity that determines the purposes and means of processing acts as a PIC, even if it handles data provided by another business partner.
items.question_text: A mobile payment gateway collects customer card data from online merchants to process payments, independently deciding fraud prevention rules and transaction retention periods. What role does the payment gateway play?
items.correct_answer: Personal Information Controller (PIC)
items.explanation: Because the gateway determines its own processing purposes, fraud algorithms, and retention rules, it acts as a PIC.

items.lesson_concept: Every PIC and PIP is required to designate an individual accountable for compliance with the DPA, commonly known as the Data Protection Officer (DPO).
items.question_text: Under NPC Circular 16-01, who is mandated to designate a Data Protection Officer?
options: Every Personal Information Controller (PIC) and Personal Information Processor (PIP)
items.correct_answer: Every Personal Information Controller (PIC) and Personal Information Processor (PIP)
items.explanation: NPC Circular 16-01 mandates that all PICs and PIPs must designate a qualified Data Protection Officer.

items.lesson_concept: A DPO must perform duties independently and without conflict of interest. Positions that determine processing purposes/means (e.g., CEO, CIO, Head of Marketing) generally cannot serve as DPO.
items.question_text: A mid-sized tech company appoints its Chief Marketing Officer (CMO) as its Data Protection Officer. Does this comply with NPC guidance?
options: Yes, any executive can serve as DPO.
No, holding both roles creates a conflict of interest since the CMO determines marketing data collection strategies.
Yes, provided the CMO takes a certification exam.
No, only licensed Philippine lawyers can become DPOs.
items.correct_answer: No, holding both roles creates a conflict of interest since the CMO determines marketing data collection strategies.
items.explanation: Under NPC guidelines, a DPO role must be free from conflicts of interest; executives who decide the purposes/means of data processing cannot serve as DPO.

items.lesson_concept: The principle of Transparency requires that data subjects be informed of the nature, purpose, and extent of the processing of their personal data.
items.question_text: Which general privacy principle requires that personal data processing policies be communicated in accessible, clear, and plain language?
items.correct_answer: Transparency
items.explanation: Transparency mandates that data subjects are informed of processing details in an accessible and easily understood manner.

items.lesson_concept: Legitimate Purpose dictates that processing must have a declared, specified, and lawful objective compatible with legal standards.
items.question_text: Which principle requires personal data to be processed solely for specific, declared purposes and not used for incompatible goals?
items.correct_answer: Legitimate Purpose
items.explanation: The principle of Legitimate Purpose requires that all processing be tied to a declared, specific, and lawful purpose.

items.lesson_concept: Proportionality ensures that data processing is adequate, relevant, suitable, necessary, and not excessive relative to the stated purpose.
items.question_text: Collecting full genetic markers from a customer subscribing to a monthly magazine subscription violates which principle?
items.correct_answer: Proportionality
items.explanation: Requiring genetic data for a simple magazine subscription is excessive and unnecessary, violating Proportionality.

items.lesson_concept: Data collected for one specific purpose cannot be repurposed for direct marketing without a separate valid lawful basis or new consent.
items.question_text: A hotel collects guest passport numbers strictly for government security compliance, then re-uses the list to send promotional spa discounts without consent. What principle is breached?
items.correct_answer: Legitimate Purpose
items.explanation: Using mandatory security registration data for promotional marketing without authorization violates Legitimate Purpose.

items.lesson_concept: The principle of Accuracy requires PICs to maintain accurate, complete, and up-to-date personal information, especially when used to make decisions.
items.question_text: A credit scoring bureau refuses to correct an erroneous loan default status on a debtor's record for two years. Which principle is violated?
items.correct_answer: Accuracy
items.explanation: Failing to maintain correct and up-to-date personal data directly violates the principle of Accuracy.

items.lesson_concept: Accountability mandates that PICs implement measures (policies, organizational controls, audits) and be able to demonstrate compliance with the DPA.
items.question_text: A company has good internal cybersecurity but maintains zero written privacy manuals, data governance logs, or staff training records. Which principle is compromised?
items.correct_answer: Accountability
items.explanation: Accountability requires demonstrating compliance through documented organizational policies, technical safeguards, and audit trails.

items.lesson_concept: Consent under the DPA must be freely given, specific, informed, and evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
items.question_text: Which of the following is an essential statutory requirement for valid consent under the DPA?
options: It can be assumed through pre-ticked checkboxes.
It must be freely given, specific, and evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
It must be notarized before a public attorney.
It must be renewed every 30 days.
items.correct_answer: It must be freely given, specific, and evidenced by written, electronic, or recorded means.
items.explanation: Section 3(b) requires consent to be freely given, specific, informed, and properly evidenced.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 12, lawful criteria for processing PI include consent, contract fulfillment, legal obligation, vital interests, public authority, and legitimate interests.
items.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a lawful basis for processing standard Personal Information under Section 12?
options: Commercial profitability of the PIC without balancing rights
Protection of vital interests of the data subject
items.correct_answer: Commercial profitability of the PIC without balancing rights
items.explanation: Commercial profit alone is not a lawful basis unless justified under a legitimate interest balancing test.

items.lesson_concept: Processing is lawful without separate consent when necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is a party.
items.question_text: An airline collects passenger full names and passport details to issue booked international flight tickets. What is the primary lawful basis?
items.correct_answer: Fulfillment of a Contract
items.explanation: Processing passenger information is necessary to fulfill the ticket purchase and carriage contract.

items.lesson_concept: Processing SPI is strictly prohibited except for statutory grounds under Section 13: consent, existing law, life/health protection, public organizations, medical treatment, or legal claims.
items.question_text: Which of the following is a recognized lawful ground for processing Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13?
options: Protection of Life and Health when subject is physically unable to express consent
items.correct_answer: Protection of Life and Health when subject is physically unable to express consent
items.explanation: Section 13(c) permits processing SPI to protect life and health when consent cannot be legally or physically given.

items.lesson_concept: Legitimate interest applies strictly to general Personal Information (Section 12) and cannot justify processing Sensitive Personal Information (Section 13).
items.question_text: An employer claims 'Legitimate Interest' to conduct genetic screenings on job applicants. Is this legally permissible?
options: Yes, if documented in internal HR manuals.
Yes, provided applicants do not verbally object.
No, Legitimate Interest is not a valid legal ground for processing Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13.
No, unless approved by the Department of Labor.
items.correct_answer: No, Legitimate Interest is not a valid legal ground for processing Sensitive Personal Information under Section 13.
items.explanation: Genetic data is SPI under Section 3(l), and Legitimate Interest cannot serve as a lawful basis under Section 13.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 13(f), processing SPI is permissible without consent when necessary for the establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims.
items.question_text: A law firm collects a defendant's past criminal history (SPI) to prepare a court defense in ongoing litigation. What is the lawful ground?
options: Establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims
items.correct_answer: Establishment, exercise, or defense of legal claims
items.explanation: Section 13(f) explicitly permits SPI processing for legal claims and court proceedings.

items.lesson_concept: The NPC Legitimate Interest Test requires three elements: Purpose Test (legitimate objective), Necessity Test (processing is necessary), and Balancing Test (does not override data subject rights).
items.question_text: What three tests must a PIC satisfy to lawfully rely on Legitimate Interest under NPC guidance?
options: Purpose Test, Necessity Test, and Balancing Test
Consent Test, Identity Test, and Disclosure Test
Security Test, Integrity Test, and Redundancy Test
items.correct_answer: Purpose Test, Necessity Test, and Balancing Test
items.explanation: The Legitimate Interest Assessment requires satisfying the Purpose, Necessity, and Balancing tests.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to be Informed guarantees that a data subject must be told whether personal data pertaining to them is being processed.
items.question_text: Which right ensures that individuals are notified before their personal data enters an automated processing system?
items.correct_answer: Right to be Informed
items.explanation: The Right to be Informed mandates notification prior to data entry into a processing system.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Access allows data subjects to demand reasonable access to contents of their personal data, sources, recipients, and reasons for disclosure.
items.question_text: What right gives a data subject the authority to request a copy of the specific personal data held by a company?
items.correct_answer: Right to Access
items.explanation: The Right to Access allows individuals to inspect and obtain copies of their personal data held by a PIC.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Object gives subjects the power to withhold or withdraw consent for processing, especially for direct marketing, profiling, or automated processing.
items.question_text: When a customer objects to data processing for direct marketing, what must the PIC do?
options: Immediately stop processing for direct marketing.
Forward the data to another processor.
items.correct_answer: Immediately stop processing for direct marketing.
items.explanation: Upon an objection to direct marketing, the PIC must immediately cease processing without exception.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Rectify allows a data subject to dispute inaccuracies or errors in personal data and have the PIC correct them immediately.
items.question_text: If a subscriber identifies a misspelled surname and incorrect address in a billing portal, which right allows them to demand immediate correction?
items.correct_answer: Right to Rectify
items.explanation: The Right to Rectify gives individuals the right to have inaccurate or outdated data corrected.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure or Blocking allows individuals to demand removal or destruction of personal data that is incomplete, outdated, false, or unlawfully obtained.
items.question_text: Under which circumstance can a data subject rightfully demand the erasure or blocking of their data?
options: When data is being used for unauthorized purposes.
When the data is needed to comply with an active court order.
When the PIC is conducting an ongoing tax audit.
When the data subject simply regrets making an authorized purchase.
items.correct_answer: When data is being used for unauthorized purposes.
items.explanation: Erasure or blocking applies when data is outdated, false, unlawfully obtained, or used for unauthorized purposes.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Erasure is not absolute and cannot be exercised when retention is required by statutory laws, court orders, or ongoing legal obligations.
items.question_text: A bank customer closes their account and demands immediate deletion of all past financial transaction records. The bank refuses, citing a 5-year AMLA record-retention rule. Is the bank justified?
options: No, the Right to Erasure is absolute upon account closure.
Yes, statutory legal obligations to retain records override the right to erasure.
No, unless the NPC grants an explicit waiver.
Yes, but only if the customer agrees in writing.
items.correct_answer: Yes, statutory legal obligations to retain records override the right to erasure.
items.explanation: Legal retention requirements (such as AMLA or tax laws) supersede the right to erasure.

items.lesson_concept: The Right to Data Portability allows data subjects to obtain their electronic data in an interoperable, structured, commonly used format.
items.question_text: Which format standard best fulfills a user's Right to Data Portability request when moving data between cloud platforms?
options: An unsearchable printed physical paper document.
A structured, commonly used, machine-readable electronic format (such as JSON or CSV).
A proprietary encrypted binary file readable only by the issuing vendor.
A scanned low-resolution JPEG of a monitor screen.
items.correct_answer: A structured, commonly used, machine-readable electronic format (such as JSON or CSV).
items.explanation: Data portability requires providing data in an electronic, structured, and commonly used machine-readable format.

items.lesson_concept: Section 17 states that lawful heirs and assigns of a data subject may invoke the data subject's rights after death or incapacity.
items.question_text: Following the sudden passing of an account holder, can their legal heirs invoke the Right to Access and Data Portability on the deceased's accounts?
options: No, privacy rights expire immediately upon death.
Yes, lawful heirs and assigns may invoke data subject rights after death or incapacity.
No, unless authorized by a presidential decree.
Yes, but strictly limited to the Right to Erasure.
items.correct_answer: Yes, lawful heirs and assigns may invoke data subject rights after death or incapacity.
items.explanation: Section 17 explicitly establishes the transmissibility of data subject rights to lawful heirs and assigns.

items.lesson_concept: The DPA prescribes criminal penalties including mandatory imprisonment and fines for violations such as unauthorized processing and negligent access.
items.question_text: What type of penalties can regular courts impose for serious offenses defined under the Data Privacy Act?
items.correct_answer: Imprisonment and criminal fines
items.explanation: Offenses under Chapter VIII of the DPA carry penal sanctions of imprisonment and substantial fines.

items.lesson_concept: Unauthorized processing of personal information without consent or statutory authority carries imprisonment from 1 to 3 years and fines.
items.question_text: What offense is committed when a database admin extracts and sells customer data without authorization or lawful basis?
items.correct_answer: Unauthorized Processing of Personal Information
items.explanation: Processing personal data without consent or legal authority constitutes the crime of Unauthorized Processing.

items.lesson_concept: Providing access to personal data due to negligence carries criminal imprisonment and fines, penalizing gross lack of basic security controls.
items.question_text: A sysadmin fails to set a password on an unencrypted public AWS S3 bucket holding employee SPI, exposing it online. Which DPA crime applies?
options: Accessing Personal Information Due to Negligence
Identity Theft under Cybercrime Act only
items.correct_answer: Accessing Personal Information Due to Negligence
items.explanation: Section 26 penalizes accessing or providing access to personal or sensitive personal information due to negligence.

items.lesson_concept: Section 30 penalizes the intentional concealment of security breaches involving personal data after having knowledge of its occurrence.
items.question_text: A security manager discovers a massive breach of sensitive financial data but deletes the incident logs to hide it from the NPC. What crime was committed?
items.correct_answer: Concealment of Security Breaches
items.explanation: Section 30 explicitly penalizes the intentional concealment of a qualifying security breach.

items.lesson_concept: Section 34 states that if the offender is a corporation, the penalty shall be imposed on responsible officers who participated in or allowed the crime through gross negligence.
items.question_text: A fintech firm is found guilty of unauthorized processing because its board ordered the bypass of privacy controls. Who incurs criminal liability?
options: Only the junior developer who wrote the code.
The responsible corporate officers who participated in or permitted the commission through gross negligence.
No individual, since the firm is a distinct juridical entity.
items.correct_answer: The responsible corporate officers who participated in or permitted the commission through gross negligence.
items.explanation: Section 34 pierces corporate liability to penalize responsible officers who directed or allowed the offense.

items.lesson_concept: NPC Circular 2022-01 authorizes administrative fines of up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income for grave infractions of the DPA and NPC issuances.
items.question_text: Under NPC Circular 2022-01, what is the maximum administrative fine the NPC can impose for grave infractions based on annual gross income?
options: Up to 1% of annual gross income
Up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income
Up to 50% of total company assets
items.correct_answer: Up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income
items.explanation: NPC Circular 2022-01 sets administrative fines for grave infractions at up to 3% to 5% of annual gross income.

items.lesson_concept: Under Section 33, when a violation involves both SPI and regular PI or constitutes a combination of multiple offenses, higher penalty brackets apply.
items.question_text: An insider steals an unencrypted database containing health records, credit card info, and home addresses, then uploads it to a leak forum for profit. What is the consequence?
options: The offense receives minimum administrative warnings.
Severe compound penalties apply for combination of offenses involving SPI and malicious disclosure.
Charges are reduced to simple civil breach of contract.
The offender receives automatic immunity by paying restitution.
items.correct_answer: Severe compound penalties apply for combination of offenses involving SPI and malicious disclosure.
items.explanation: Section 33 mandates higher, compounded criminal penalties when multiple DPA offenses and SPI are involved.

items.lesson_concept: A security incident affects system CIA (confidentiality, integrity, availability), whereas a personal data breach specifically compromises personal data.
items.question_text: What distinguishes a Personal Data Breach from a general Security Incident?
options: A data breach involves actual or reasonable belief of unauthorized compromise of personal data.
A security incident only involves hardware fires.
A data breach never involves software bugs.
They are 100% identical in all legal aspects.
items.correct_answer: A data breach involves actual or reasonable belief of unauthorized compromise of personal data.
items.explanation: A personal data breach is a specific security incident resulting in unlawful access, destruction, loss, or alteration of personal data.

items.lesson_concept: NPC Circular 16-03 mandates notification to the NPC and affected data subjects within 72 hours of knowledge or reasonable belief of a qualifying breach.
items.question_text: Within what mandatory timeframe must a PIC notify the NPC upon reasonable belief of a qualifying personal data breach?
items.correct_answer: 72 hours
items.explanation: Section 20(f) of the DPA and NPC Circular 16-03 establish a strict 72-hour notification timeline.

items.lesson_concept: Mandatory breach notification requires ALL three: 1) involves SPI/financial info, 2) unauthorized acquisition occurred, 3) poses real risk of serious harm.
items.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three mandatory criteria triggering the 72-hour notification under NPC Circular 16-03?
options: Sensitive Personal Information or identity fraud data is involved.
Data was acquired by an unauthorized person.
The company's stock price dropped by at least 10%.
The breach poses a real risk of serious harm to data subjects.
items.correct_answer: The company's stock price dropped by at least 10%.
items.explanation: Stock performance is irrelevant; notification is triggered by sensitive data, unauthorized acquisition, and real risk of serious harm.

items.lesson_concept: The Incident Response Life Cycle consists of Preparation, Detection and Analysis, Containment/Eradication/Recovery, and Post-Incident Activity.
items.question_text: In the Incident Response Life Cycle, in which phase does an organization isolate affected network segments to stop ongoing data exfiltration?
items.correct_answer: Containment, Eradication, and Recovery
items.explanation: Isolating compromised systems to stop data leaks occurs during the Containment, Eradication, and Recovery phase.

items.lesson_concept: A temporary system outage (availability breach) without unauthorized acquisition or real risk of serious harm does not trigger mandatory 72-hour NPC notification.
items.question_text: A power surge shuts down a university server for 3 hours. Internal logs confirm no data was altered or accessed by unauthorized third parties. Is a 72-hour NPC notification required?
options: Yes, all outages require 72-hour NPC notification.
No, because no data was acquired by an unauthorized party creating a risk of serious harm.
Yes, but only to the local police.
No, but all student IDs must be immediately re-issued.
items.correct_answer: No, because no data was acquired by an unauthorized party creating a risk of serious harm.
items.explanation: Without unauthorized acquisition or risk of serious harm, mandatory 72-hour reporting is not triggered, though it must be logged internally.

items.lesson_concept: If a stolen device contains encrypted data where the decryption key remains uncompromised, the risk of harm is mitigated, potentially exempting from data subject notice.
items.question_text: A company laptop containing biometric data is stolen, but full-disk AES-256 encryption is active and the key is secure. What is the notification obligation under NPC Circular 16-03?
options: Mandatory public TV broadcast within 24 hours.
The incident is logged; notification to data subjects may be exempted if encryption prevents unauthorized access.
Immediate filing of criminal charges against the employee.
items.correct_answer: The incident is logged; notification to data subjects may be exempted if encryption prevents unauthorized access.
items.explanation: Under NPC Circular 16-03, strong encryption that renders data unreadable to unauthorized parties can exempt the PIC from notifying data subjects.

items.lesson_concept: All security incidents—whether qualifying for mandatory 72-hour notice or not—must be documented in an internal incident log and summarized in an Annual Security Incident Report to the NPC.
items.question_text: Must a PIC document minor security incidents (e.g., thwarted phishing emails, minor temporary glitches) that did not require a 72-hour breach notice?
options: No, minor incidents can be discarded immediately.
Yes, all security incidents must be documented internally and submitted annually in the Annual Security Incident Report.
Only if requested by a court order.
No, only criminal convictions require documentation.
items.correct_answer: Yes, all security incidents must be documented internally and submitted annually in the Annual Security Incident Report.
items.explanation: NPC Circular 16-03 requires maintaining internal records of all incidents and submitting an Annual Security Incident Report to the NPC.

items.lesson_concept: When a PIP experiences a data breach, it must notify the PIC immediately without unreasonable delay to enable the PIC to meet its 72-hour NPC reporting window.
items.question_text: A third-party cloud hosting provider (PIP) discovers a breach of patient data belonging to a hospital client (PIC). What is the PIP's legal duty regarding notification?
options: The PIP can wait 30 days before emailing the hospital.
The PIP must notify the hospital (PIC) immediately without unreasonable delay.
The PIP bypasses the hospital and files an exclusive report without informing the hospital.
The PIP is immune from reporting obligations.
items.correct_answer: The PIP must notify the hospital (PIC) immediately without unreasonable delay.
items.explanation: A PIP must notify the PIC without unreasonable delay so the PIC can fulfill its 72-hour statutory notification obligations to the NPC and affected data subjects.
